title: Large language models as optimizers
venue: The Twelfth International Conference on Learning Representations

publication.venue: The Twelfth International Conference on Learning Representations

mechanism.domainTask: General black-box optimization and natural-language prompt optimization
mechanism.populationDetail: Maintains a score-sorted optimization trajectory of multiple solutions; prompt optimization typically exposes the best 20 within the meta-prompt.
mechanism.archiveDetail: The meta-prompt includes a top-scoring subset from history (best 20 in the default prompt-optimization experiments), but this is trajectory context rather than a formally named archive.
mechanism.replacementDetail: New solution-score pairs are appended to the trajectory; context-length limits filter the prompt to top candidates. This is memory/trajectory-based optimization, not a conventional evolutionary population update.
mechanism.generationDetail: The optimizer is asked to generate a new solution from the task description and prior solution-score trajectory, rather than edit a selected parent.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Past scalar scores are part of the primary optimization trajectory, not additional evaluator metadata.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: No true editable parent is selected; prior scored candidates are contextual examples, with a top-k subset included in prompt optimization.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: General trajectory-conditioned black-box optimization rather than canonical population-based evolutionary search.

provenance.citationWarning: Survey currently cites OPRO as a single-model example, but the original paper evaluates both same-model and distinct optimizer/scorer backbones (Table 4); role/configuration variability should be reflected. Other chapter placements describe transferable optimizer mechanisms, not evidence that OPRO is a canonical LLM-ES population method.
